text: Paul Kubit is a Blizzard employee and Senior Game Designer on World of Warcraft, focusing on professions. He has previously worked on Diablo III and Starcraft II, including providing "monster voice effects" for Diablo III. Kubit joined Blizzard around 2006, working in Q&A. He later worked on World of Warcraft as a Quest Designer, from Cataclysm until Warlords of Draenor, before moving into professions with Legion, describing himself as "point person" for professions content in the expansion.

Peafowl are colorful birds found on both Azeroth and the , notable for their fan-like tail feathers. Adult males are called peacocks, females are peahens, and young are peachicks. Azerothian peafowl are mainly found in Thaldraszus on the Dragon Isles, but also parts of the Waking Shores and the Azure Span. Draenic peachicks can mainly be found as critters in Talador, the Spires of Arak, and the Everbloom. A single peacock feather is often laid upon a grave to ward off evil spirits. The bloodfeather type is completely fearless and will charge any threat with fanned-out feathers. The feathers of the golden dawnfeather type are said to glitter like gold in the rising sun.

Patton did research on how to portray the role.

Peeling is generally used to refer to either a player or mob being removed from another player. There are two types of peels. The first type of peel usually involves another player intercepting and gaining aggro from a given mob (in essence, "peeling" the mob off that player) who is attacking one of the more squishy members of the group. This role or action is most commonly filled by a Hunter in the raid environment where peeling mobs off an initial aggro target to a tank is a common step in the pulling of many boss encounters that have multiple mobs involved. .]] Peons are the laborers and lumberjacks of the Horde and orcish clans. Cowardly, lazy, and slow-witted, they are typically unfit for warfare, but their work is simply indispensable. Without them, more able-bodied orcs would have to take precious time from their battles to do menial labor. This is why the importance of the peon is recognized in the holiday Peon Day. Even so, long years of service take a harsh toll, as most peons are physically bent from beatings and hard work. They trudge expressionlessly in their duty, a large sack slouched over malformed shoulders that are broader than any soldier's. Peons appeared as units on the Horde side in Warcraft I, Warcraft II, and Warcraft III,
